clue.text: Reddish-brown fungus found around the Kent area

indicators.note: the fungus word is located on either side of the area's letters

parts.note: rust is a fungal disease of plants
Kent is a county in the south-east corner of England, abbreviated SE

explanation.surface: A mushroom hunter reports a rusty-coloured toadstool growing in the Kentish countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found around' is the container signal. Kent sits in the south-east corner of England, so setters use it for that compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: A colour name: the warm brown with a red tinge seen on some apples and autumn leaves.

clue.text: Strain undergone by Lawrence, latterly, in this carriage?

indicators.note: in a down clue the strain sits on top, with Lawrence's later name going under it

parts.note: to rick a muscle or one's neck is to strain or sprain it
T. E. Lawrence (of Arabia) took the surname Shaw late in life

explanation.surface: Lawrence of Arabia, in his later years, suffered some stress while riding in a carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undergone by' places the second piece beneath the first in this down entry. T. E. Lawrence legally became T. E. Shaw in 1927.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a light two-wheeled passenger vehicle pulled by a person, common in Asia.

clue.text: Second rise for teachers has a man dumbfounded

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the teachers' letters are written upwards

parts.note: the NUT was the National Union of Teachers, a British trade union
Ned is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man is left speechless when teachers win a second pay increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise for' sends NUT up the grid as TUN. The NUT was Britain's National Union of Teachers.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both describe someone shocked into speechlessness.

clue.text: Steak dish taken in bed? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: one piece is swallowed by the other; read straight, the dish would go inside the bed
swaps the roles just stated, so the bed goes inside the dish instead

parts.note: an entree is a dish or course of a meal
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys the luxury of a steak dinner eaten in bed, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' first suggests the dish goes inside the bed; 'Quite the opposite' flips that, so the bed goes inside the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a boned cut of beef from between the ribs, served grilled or fried.

clue.text: High award for army officer held by a rebel leader

indicators.note: the officer is gripped inside the letters of the other two pieces

parts.note: Jack Cade led the Kentish rebellion of 1450 against Henry VI
Col is the abbreviation for colonel

explanation.surface: A leader of the rebels holds a top decoration meant for an officer in the army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' is the container signal. Jack Cade led an English popular revolt in 1450, a favourite rebel of crossword setters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an honour or mark of great praise bestowed on someone.

clue.text: Studies obvious truth about endlessly active art movement

parts.note: to con is an old verb meaning to study or learn, so studies is cons

indicators.note: the truth word goes round the trimmed word

parts.note: a truism is a statement too plainly true to need saying

indicators.note: having no ends, the word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Research into a plain fact concerning a tirelessly busy school of artists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' strips both ends of 'active' and 'about' wraps the truth round what is left. 'Studies' is a verb here, from the old word con, to learn.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the abstract, industrial style that arose in Russia around 1915.

clue.text: Bizarre form of 24

indicators.note: another form of a word is its letters shaped differently

parts.note: a cross-reference: the solution at 24 down is OUTER

explanation.surface: An odd variety of whatever is at number twenty-four.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' rearranges the five letters of the solution to 24 down, so that clue has to be cracked first.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym, borrowed from French: unconventional to the point of being strange.

clue.text: Arrest English diplomat

parts.note: in law, to attach a person or goods is to seize them by authority

explanation.surface: An order to take an English envoy into custody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrest' is used in its legal sense: attachment is the seizure of a person or property by court order.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a specialist official on an embassy's staff.

clue.text: An inch, do we hear, this small hole?

indicators.note: asks whether the word for an inch, when spoken, matches the hole's name

parts.note: inch is a Scottish word for a small island, an islet

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a tiny hole measures just an inch across.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do we hear' signals the sound-alike. 'Inch' is no measurement here: in Scotland and Ireland an inch is a small island, as in Inchcolm.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a little ring-edged opening for a lace or cord to pass through.

clue.text: Uniformed attendant gets cut when on river

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece stands on top of the river

parts.note: a cut is a share of the takings, such as an agent's commission
the Aire is a river in Yorkshire, flowing through Leeds

explanation.surface: A doorman in livery is injured while boating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when on' stacks the cut above the river in this down entry. The Aire is a Yorkshire river.
explanation.definitionFit: A British term for the liveried doorman at a hotel, theatre or cinema.

clue.text: Numbers backing the start of a mission

definitions.text: Numbers backing the start of a mission

parts.words: Numbers backing the start of a mission
parts.note: backing means going backwards: figures called in descending order just before a rocket launch

explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical description: the figures run backwards to zero before a space launch.

clue.text: In part it helped to stock this barn

definitions.note: the word that goes before barn to name the building where a parish's tenth of produce was stored

indicators.note: the letters sit unbroken inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A portion of something once helped to fill a farm building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' shows the word lies inside 'part it helped'. The whole clue also describes it: the tenth of produce paid to the church was kept in such a barn.
explanation.definitionFit: The word completes the name of a barn built to hold the parish's tenth of the harvest.

clue.text: Ray gives retiring seamen support

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the seamen's letters run backwards

parts.note: the NUS was the National Union of Seamen, a British trade union
a beam is a timber or girder that supports a structure

explanation.surface: A man called Ray lends his backing to sailors leaving the service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' turns NUS into SUN. The NUS was Britain's National Union of Seamen.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a shaft of light from the sky.

clue.text: Sweetener a politician left in box, perhaps

indicators.note: the three short pieces are placed inside the box word

parts.note: box is one kind of tree, an evergreen used for hedging
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A bribe that a politician carelessly abandoned in a container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A, C and L inside TREE. 'Box' is the evergreen shrub, not a container. The answer is the British name for molasses-like syrup.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the thick dark syrup, called molasses in America, used to sweeten puddings.

clue.text: A posh woman has overhead sound reproduction

parts.note: U is the label for upper-class speech and manners
Di is a woman's name, short for Diana
read as two words, over head: the head, or leading letter, of the word over

explanation.surface: An upper-class lady has a hi-fi system installed above her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overhead' must be read as 'over head', the leading letter of 'over'. U for upper-class comes from the 1950s U and non-U labels.
explanation.definitionFit: The term covers recorded or broadcast sound and the equipment that plays it.

clue.text: Comparatively dumpy person in illegal occupation

definitions.meaning: the comparative form of an adjective meaning short and thickset
someone living in a building or on land without any right to

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: more short and thickset, and someone occupying property unlawfully.

clue.text: Actor shamefully lit up at first in the plant

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go at the front, before the actor
behaving shamefully is behaving badly, so the letters are out of order

parts.note: Sir Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a famous Victorian actor-manager

explanation.surface: A performer disgraces himself by turning up drunk at the factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shamefully' is the anagram signal and 'at first' sets the result in front. Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a great Victorian actor-manager; 'plant' is no factory.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a North American member of the magnolia family with cup-shaped flowers.

clue.text: It sounds as if Miss Oakley has fixed a drink

indicators.note: the phrase that follows is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: Annie Oakley was the American sharpshooter; has fixed is set, giving Annie set

explanation.surface: By the noise of it, Annie Oakley has mixed herself a cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It sounds as if' signals the sound-alike: say 'Annie set' and the liqueur is heard.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a sweet liqueur flavoured with aniseed.

clue.text: It turned out extremely vain, Eliot's occupation

indicators.note: turned out suggests the letters are tipped out and rearranged
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: all six letters are used, the possessive S included

explanation.surface: Writing proved a futile calling for someone named Eliot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' rearranges VN ('extremely' taking the first and last letters of 'vain') with ELIOTS. The whole clue hints at the answer too: it was George Eliot's job.
explanation.definitionFit: An example of a profession, and the very one George Eliot followed.

clue.text: 16 may have bowed when this lutenist sang

parts.words: 16 may have bowed when this lutenist sang
parts.note: alludes to Shakespeare's song in Henry VIII, where a mythical musician with his lute made trees bow themselves when he did sing; 16 down is a tree

explanation.definitionFit: The Greek mythical musician whose playing charmed trees, beasts and stones.

clue.text: Almost like Mowgli's brothers to make such a bloomer!

indicators.note: almost the whole word: its final letter is dropped

parts.note: in Kipling's Jungle Book Mowgli is raised by wolves, and lupine means wolf-like

explanation.surface: Behaving nearly as wildly as the Jungle Book cubs leads to an embarrassing blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts the last letter from LUPINE. 'Bloomer' looks like British slang for a blunder but means something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a garden flower with tall coloured spikes.

clue.text: Politic to observe simple direction during training

indicators.note: the two pieces fall inside the span of the training letters

parts.note: PT is physical training
rude can mean simple or roughly made, as in a rude shelter
N is north, a compass direction

explanation.surface: It is wise to follow a straightforward instruction while being trained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' is the container signal. 'Politic' is the adjective meaning shrewd, not short for politics, and 'simple' has its old sense of unsophisticated.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: sensible and judicious in practical matters.

clue.text: In Egypt, a reason for pandemonium

indicators.note: the reason word is placed inside the country's letters

parts.note: Egypt was officially the United Arab Republic, UAR, from 1958 to 1971
a pro is an argument or reason in favour, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: Something in Cairo gives cause for chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is the container signal. Egypt was officially the United Arab Republic from 1958 to 1971, current history when solvers of this puzzle were young.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both mean a noisy, chaotic commotion.

clue.text: Make noise like a gun to preserve the maize

parts.note: a gun going off is said to pop
to corn meat is to preserve it with salt, as in corned beef

explanation.surface: A farmer fires off bangs to scare birds and protect the crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corn' as a verb means to cure with salt. The whole clue also describes how the snack is made, with the kernels bursting noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a variety of the cereal whose kernels burst when heated.

clue.text: Old-fashioned king gets shot

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion
ER is Edwardus Rex, the royal cipher of King Edward

explanation.surface: A monarch with dated ways is gunned down.
explanation.walkthrough: ER as a king is Edwardus Rex, the cipher of the Edwards. In target shooting an outer is a hit on the outermost ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A target-shooting term: a hit on the ring farthest from the bull.

clue.text: Virginia comes down with depression

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for the state of Virginia
when rain comes down heavily it pours

explanation.surface: A woman called Virginia falls ill with low spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the old-fashioned phrase 'the vapours', a fit of low spirits or faintness.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic term for a bout of low spirits or nervous faintness.

clue.text: When one is missing, the implication is plain

indicators.note: the three letters of the number are absent from the longer word

parts.note: an overtone is a subtle suggested meaning
one, taken as written

explanation.surface: If somebody fails to turn up, what that suggests is obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is missing' takes ONE off the end of OVERTONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: open and unconcealed, obvious to all.

clue.text: Strong desire to replace volunteers in immediate rising

indicators.note: the desire takes the place of the volunteers' letters in the longer word

parts.note: instant means happening at once
the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
an urge is a powerful wish or impulse

explanation.surface: There is keen eagerness to swap the part-time soldiers at once during a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to replace' swaps the TA in INSTANT for URGE. The TA is Britain's Territorial Army of volunteers. 'Rising' is an adjective here: in revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective both describe people rebelling against authority.

clue.text: Book finally read when retiring

parts.note: to book a table or seat is to reserve it

indicators.note: the final letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone at last gets through a novel as they go off to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes the last letter of 'read'. 'Retiring' is not going to bed but being shy.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: shy, reticent and slow to show feelings.

clue.text: Pay to remove article from American city

indicators.note: an instruction to take the article out of the place name

parts.note: Seattle is a city in Washington State
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone is charged a fee for taking an item away from a town in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to remove' takes the A out of SEATTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to discharge a bill or debt.
